meta.title: Who's Bluffing? — Find out who's bluffing.

landing.lead: Pick answers, say how sure you are, and find out whether your confidence matches what you actually know.
landing.consent: 5 minutes. Anonymous — no account, no tracking. Your answers go into a public research dataset. Close the page any time to stop.
landing.teach: I teach — create a class code
landing.code_bad: A class code is 6 letters or digits.
landing.code_unknown: We couldn't find that class code. Check it with your teacher.
landing.code_offline: We couldn't check the code. Check your connection and try again.

test.range_intro: Give a range you are 90% sure contains the answer.
test.need_numbers: Enter a number in both boxes.
test.swap: The From number is bigger than the To number. Press the button again and we’ll swap them.
test.unusual: That looks unusual for this question. Check the unit ({unit}), or press the button again to keep it.

demo.title: Four optional questions
demo.lead: They let the research compare groups. Skip them if you like.

region.oceania: Australia, New Zealand or the Pacific

results.title: Your results
results.int_headline: Your 90% ranges were right {k} of {n} times.
results.int_explain: Ranges you are truly 90% sure of contain the answer about 9 times in 10: 5 or 6 out of 6.
results.over_headline: You were {x} points more confident than you were right.
results.under_headline: You were {x} points less confident than you were right.
results.even_headline: Your confidence matched how often you were right.
results.conf_explain: On the two-choice questions your average confidence was {c}% and you got {a}% right. The difference, {x}, is your overconfidence score: 0 means your confidence matched your accuracy, above 0 means overconfident, below 0 means underconfident.
results.chart_title: How sure you were vs. how often you were right
results.chart_note: Dots below the dashed line mean you were more sure than right.
results.pct_over: You were more overconfident than {p}% of people who took the test.
results.pct_int: Your ranges caught the answer more often than {p}% of them.
results.global: {n} people in {k} countries have taken the test so far.

share.title: Share your result
share.copy_failed: Couldn't copy. Select the link and copy it yourself.
share.long_press: On a phone, press and hold the image to save it.

class.title: Use Who's Bluffing in class
class.lead: Students take the test on their phones while you watch the class's confidence curve build live. No accounts. You see only class totals, never anyone's answers, and nothing until 5 students have finished.
class.label: Class name (optional)
class.create_failed: Couldn't create a class code. Try again.
class.private: Anyone with the dashboard link can see the class totals. Bookmark it now: there is no way to get it back later.
class.project_1: 1. Put this on the screen: open {url} on your phone and enter code {code}.
class.project_2: 2. Open your dashboard on the projector. The class chart appears once 5 students have finished.

dash.title: Class dashboard
dash.waiting: Waiting for 5 students — {n} finished so far.
dash.int_hit: 90% ranges contained the answer {h}% of the time

stats.title: Live stats
stats.curve_title: Everyone: how sure vs. how often right
stats.row: {n} people · average overconfidence {x} points · 90% ranges right {h}% of the time
stats.note: Counts only sessions that passed both attention checks. Updated every minute.
stats.failed: Couldn't load the stats. Try again later.
stats.kpi_detail: As of {date} (UTC), updated once a day. Monthly players by surface: web {web}, Slack {slack}, Discord {discord}, rooms {room}, classroom {classroom}. Communities: {workspaces} Slack workspaces, {guilds} Discord servers, {rooms} rooms and {classrooms} classrooms.
stats.kpi_empty: Player counts appear once the daily update has run.
stats.anki: Anki add-on installations that shared ratings in the last 30 days: {n} (counted separately, not part of MAU).
stats.mau_definition: MAU: anonymous ids with ≥ 1 play — a completed round of 10 (ranked or quick), a completed full assessment, or an in-channel Slack or Discord answer to the daily question — in the trailing 30 days, summed across web, Slack and Discord without cross-surface deduplication (a person who plays on two surfaces counts twice). DAU likewise for one UTC day.
stats.communities_definition: Communities: Slack workspaces, Discord servers and rooms with ≥ 1 play in the trailing 30 days, plus classrooms with ≥ 5 finished assessments; reported per platform and summed.
stats.daily_empty: No one has finished today’s game yet.
stats.engagement_rounds_def: Rounds per player per day: completed rounds divided by the days on which each player finished at least one round, over the trailing 30 days.
stats.engagement_return_def: Day-1 and day-7 return rates by first-play cohort: of the players whose first play fell in the 30 days before, the share who played again exactly 1 or 7 days later.
stats.engagement_challenge_def: Challenge conversion (completed rounds per challenge view): rounds finished from a challenge link, divided by challenge page views, over the trailing 30 days.
stats.engagement_share_def: Share rate (share events per completed round): each Copy result, Share, Download or Copy image tap counts once, divided by completed rounds, over the trailing 30 days.
stats.engagement_note: A dash means there is nothing to divide by yet.
stats.ranked_empty: No one has finished today’s ranked round yet.

daily.title: Who's Bluffing? #{number}
daily.lead: Five questions, the same for everyone today. For each one, give a range you are 90% sure contains the answer.
daily.consent: About a minute. Anonymous — no account, no tracking. Your answers go into a public research dataset.
daily.full_note: Want the 5-minute version with a calibration chart?
daily.offline: We couldn’t reach the server. Your answer is still here.
daily.failed: Couldn’t load today’s game. Check your connection and try again.
daily.no_game: There’s no game today. Come back tomorrow, or take the full assessment.
daily.note_hit: Caught it. Ranges you are truly 90% sure of catch about 9 answers in 10.
daily.note_above: The answer was above your range. Misses like this usually mean the range was too narrow.
daily.note_below: The answer was below your range. Misses like this usually mean the range was too narrow.
daily.flag_thanks: Thanks. A question reported by several players is taken out and checked.
daily.flag_failed: Couldn’t send the report. Try again later.
daily.result_explain: If your ranges were truly 90% sure, you would catch 4 or 5 on most days.
daily.hist_title: How many ranges each player caught today
daily.come_back: A new game every day at midnight UTC.

rounds.type_hedger: Much less sure than right: 15 or more points under your accuracy.
rounds.chart_note: Each dot is one confidence level; dots below the dashed line mean you were surer than right.
